description: Governed REGISTER vocabulary — the course-level voice coordinate a rendering of meaning is written to: who the words are for and how they are pitched (stance, person, formality). Register is a coordinate in the same rendering space as locale: voice packs (voice/<register>.json) sit beside locale packs (locales/<lang>.json) as sibling store families, both keyed by atom_id, both gated against the atom's content_hash. Dragoman owns this whole space; language and register are coordinates, and each of its modes declares its own gate profile (see DECISIONS 2026-08-31, voice-pack contract block).

governance.rule: A voice pack may only declare a register id defined here. A new register requires a version bump and an entry — the validator rejects anything else. Per-register `status` additionally gates AUTHORING: only a `specified` register may carry accepted renderings; renderings authored against a `draft` register are flagged by the gate, not silently admitted.
governance.supplants: Nothing — first vocabulary of the rendering-coordinate family.

boundaries.tone: Register is NOT tone (vocab/tone.enum.json). Tone is per-element affect at the intent layer — what feeling THIS element carries, varying scene to scene, set upstream and read by the realizer. Register is the course-level voice coordinate — constant across a rendering. TONE MODULATES WITHIN REGISTER: the voice writer reads each element's tone as an input while writing every entry to one register. Neither vocabulary absorbs the other.
boundaries.locale: Register does not translate. The spec fields below are ABSTRACT intent, realized natively per locale — conversational Japanese is not translated conversational English. When a locale rendering chains from a voice rendering, the voiced source text transmits the authored choices, this spec transmits the shared intent, and the atom remains the judge.
boundaries.audience: Register is a coordinate someone CHOOSES for a course — a governed input the voice writer writes to. Which learner segment gets which register is the audience facet's join (Chameleon), downstream. The voice writer never reasons about who the learners are; the moment it does, single-writer has broken.

spec_fields.person: Grammatical person of address the register intends (e.g. second_direct, impersonal).
spec_fields.stance: The writer's posture toward the learner (e.g. learner_advocate, neutral_authority).
spec_fields.formality: Formality intent, not surface rules (e.g. conversational_professional, formal).

values.label: Warm & Direct
values.provenance: Reverse-specified 2026-08-31 from the January artisan control course (cgen/courses/brunswick_pay_transparency_employee/course.json) — the voice-pack arc's validation target.
values.definition: Second-person, plain-language, reassuring learner advocacy. Compresses source meaning into copy that addresses the learner directly and lowers threat.
observed_markers: Direct address and possessives: 'What It Means for You', 'your pay'.
Contractions and plain diction: 'wasn't', 'It's a system, not a judgment.'
De-threatening reassurance moves: 'No trick questions', 'a solid, positive place to be'.
Rights-affirming persuade beats: 'You have every right to understand your pay.'
Compression: on-screen copy far terser than source; narration fuller but still conversational.
